claims.text: NESDIS is lift-and-shift migrating all NCEI data, products and services from the Asheville and Boulder servers to AWS in waves through spring 2027, then into the NESDIS Common Cloud Framework, and plans to decommission the on-premises IT as capabilities move.

evidence.passage: In one of the largest undertakings in its history, NESDIS is migrating all of its data, products, and services to the cloud through Spring 2027. Data and applications housed in servers at locations in Asheville, North Carolina and Boulder, Colorado, are being migrated (moved) in waves to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud. … The cloud migration is using a process known as “lift and shift”. … Teams that include NOAA experts are also ensuring that all of the critical products customers rely on are functioning after the “lift and shift,” and the integrity of the data is maintained. | Immediately upon completion of the “lift and shift,” NESDIS specialists will enter into a “modernization and optimization” phase, integrating seamlessly into the NESDIS Cloud System and Common Cloud Framework. … Occasional and temporary data delays may occur throughout the 10-month process … Archival packages may take longer to process and publish during this transition; however, all data submissions are still securely being staged in queue to be archived and there is no risk of data data loss.
evidence.location: sections 'When is the data being moved', 'How does the migration work', 'Data Archival Delays'

evidence.passage: Current Impact: Many access portals, interactive maps, and data folders are currently unavailable due to the migration. Expect delayed data archival and slower update cycles for many products. … No datasets will be retired as part of the cloud migration. Please note that several NCEI datasets were retired over the last 18 months. … Data formats will not change; however, many datasets will also be available in cloud native formats such as Zarr, Parquet, and GeoJSON after the migration. … Bulk data folders will move from web accessible folders (WAFs) to Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3).

Continue a strategic and prioritized transition of environmental data ingest, preservation, access, and use-inspired | information/services to the NESDIS Common Cloud Framework (NCCF) … Decommission on premises information technology infrastructure commensurate with the successful transition of archive, | access, and information production/service capabilities to the NCCF … It hosts and provides access to over 70 petabytes (PB) of data (primary and secure copy), projected to increase annually by | 8.5 PB in 2030.

NOAA calls them 'ten year contracts' with option periods; Google's has 'the potential to span 10 years'. Providers may charge for compute but must give free access to the data. No end date or termination clause is published, so hosting depends on NOAA exercising options.

evidence.passage: The NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD) Program started out as the Big Data Project in April 2015 (and then later became Big Data Program), when NOAA signed three year Non-competitive Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (CRADAs) with Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, IBM, Microsoft Azure, and the Open Common Consortium. The CRADA was later extended for an extra year ending May 4, 2019. … May 2019 - CRADA ends | September 2019 - Operational phase begins | October 2019 - First year of BDP Initial Operating Capability (IOC)

In 2019, NOAA began the formal process to operationalize the BDP and formally requested proposals from industry, which resulted in signed ten year contracts with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft. This resulted in the Big Data Project becoming the Big Data Program with initial BDP operational capability beginning in October 2019. | In 2021, the BDP became an operational enterprise service known as NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD) with a continued mission to provide the public with free and easy data access via the cloud. These unique contracts memorialize NODD's public–private partnerships with the CSPs … The NOAA datasets made available through NODD are free for all users to access with no use restrictions and do not require any registration to access. The data is fully open for public access and can be downloaded with no egress charges.
evidence.location: FAQ: history answer and 'What are the costs' answer

evidence.passage: NOAA and Google signed a contract with the potential to span 10 years

December 19, 2019 … NOAA has entered into separate multiyear contracts with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft to provide the public with cloud-based access to the agency's environmental data sets … Under the contracts, the cloud platform providers can charge for compute or other services related to additional processing of NOAA data, but are required to provide free and open access to the data itself. … Rather than utilize a traditional, large-value contract award, these contracts represent a unique relationship with the Cloud Service Providers: NOAA contributes its high-quality environmental information and scientific expertise, and the CSPs provide their cloud storage and technical capabilities, improving the public's ability to use these data without being charged for cloud storage or data access. … the contract awardees were selected through a Request for Proposal conducted in spring 2019.

SO. 3.3: Big Data Program (BDP) - NOAA signed contracts with three Cloud Service Providers in late FY20. The BDP team successfully transitioned from Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) to the BDP contracts in Jan of 2020 … SO. 3.3: Big Data Program (BDP) - NOAA anticipates executing option period one of the BDP contract if there are no contract performance issues during FY20 and FY21. During FY22, BDP plans to continue expanding its data holdings and increasing the amount of data that is being stored under the 15PB BDP allocation.

ID = 11 character station identification code. … YEAR/MONTH/DAY = 8 character date in YYYYMMDD format … ELEMENT = 4 character indicator of element type … DATA VALUE = 5 character data value for ELEMENT … M-FLAG = 1 character Measurement Flag … Q-FLAG = 1 character Quality Flag … S-FLAG = 1 character Source Flag … OBS-TIME = 4-character time of observation in hour-minute format … PRCP = Precipitation (tenths of mm) … TMAX = Maximum temperature (tenths of degrees C) … The data set is updated daily. … arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123901341784:NewGHCNObject
